Abstract
Metro Integrated Supervision and Control System (MISCS) belongs to the category of integrated automation of electrome-
chanical equipment of urban rail transit, through establishing the monitoring and control of each electromechanical equipment
system, making its operation within the controllable scope, providing emergency treatment plan and rich information for safe
operation and dispatching command, so as to ensure the safety and high efﬁciency of metro operation. rich information, so as
to ensure the safety and high efﬁciency of metro operation. Aiming at the operation and scheduling pressure existing in the
existing MISCS, a cloud-side cooperative optimization scheduling method for MISCS based on edge computing is designed
by taking advantage of the real-time analysis and fast calculation of edge computing technology and relying on the cloud-side
cooperative architecture. Using edge-side monitoring data ubiquitous sensing, edge node data feature analysis, panoramic
monitoring visualization technology, optimizing the existing MISCS operation mode, designing the operation optimization
scheme of the ground body integrated monitoring system applying edge computing technology, and targeting the problem of
the current metro integrated monitoring system covering a wide range of areas and having too many tasks, which leads to
the system latency being too high, under the cloud-edge cooperative architecture, we propose a simulated annealing-based
Simulated-annealing-based Adaptive Genetic Taboo Search Algorithm (SAGTSA) computational ofﬂoading strategy, which
enables the scheduling tasks of the MISCS to adaptively adjust the ofﬂoading strategy of migrating to the edge nodes or cloud
center. According to the characteristics of task scheduling, a scheduling method based on improved pointer network (IPN) is
designed for scheduling ISCS tasks after the computational ofﬂoading strategy based on SAGTSA is proposed. Simulation
results show that the method proposed in this paper, the method proposed in this paper has ideal timeliness, is better than other
methods in achieving the efﬁciency of scheduling computational tasks, effectively improves the operational performance of
MISCS, and helps to enhance the stability of metro operation.
Keywords MISCS · SAGTSA · IPN · Cloud-side cooperative · Optimization scheduling · Edge computing

tion collection equipment at the edge end generates a huge

information and data are transmitted to the cloud computing

continuous deployment of monitoring equipment, the sys-
tem can only rely on the simple and repetitive increase in the
number of the with the continuous deployment of monitoring
equipment, it is only by simply and repeatedly increasing the
number of center servers and upgrading performance param-
eters to meet the demand, which increases the resources and
costs for new system construction, old system transformation
and application [7].
Previously, cloud computing technology has been used
due to its high reliability and scalability, however, ofﬂoading
all the big data to the cloud platform may lead to network con-
gestion, which reduces the overall Quality of Service (QoS)
of various applications [8]. To alleviate the network conges-
tion caused by big data, the industry proposes to introduce
another technology to provide computational processing and
data storage capabilities by deploying edge nodes at the edge
of the network, i.e., edge computing. Cloud computing and
edge computing are complementary to each other, and the
cloud-edge cooperative technology can fully combine the
advantages of cloud centers and edge nodes to jointly sched-
ule services with different characteristics, so the introduction
of cloud-edge cooperative technology into MISCS has high
research value and application signiﬁcance. With the gradual
development and maturity of edge computing technology, it
provides technical conditions for intelligent monitoring in
metro. Edge computing technology is to provide edge intel-
ligent services close to the edge side of the network near
the object or data source, close to mobile devices or sensors.
The edge node performs certain operations and processing
on the data, and then transmits the reﬁned data to the cloud
after processing. The amount of data sent to the cloud after
processing has been greatly reduced, which can achieve the
purpose of reducing the pressure on the cloud and solving
the network delay and bandwidth limitations.

The main contributions of this paper are as follows: (1)
Based on the current MISCS structure, a novel SAGTSA
algorithm is designed to process the tasks received by the
edge nodes and realize the automatic ofﬂoading decision. (2)
An edge cloud cooperative architecture is designed to reduce
the computational latency of the tasks by leaving a portion of
the tasks to be processed at the edge nodes while the tasks are
being processed and uploading all the remaining tasks to the
cloud center for processing. (3) A scheduling optimization

Related work
Computation ofﬂoading is a technological advantage of edge
computing, through which the execution delay of computa-
tional tasks can be reduced to satisfy users’ computational
needs. Xing et al. [9] investigated a multi-assisted MEC sys-
tem supporting device-to-device communication with the
optimization objective of reducing the latency of compu-
tational tasks, modeling the problem as a mixed-integer
nonlinear programming problem. Considering the additional
delays caused by random arrivals of tasks and service migra-
tions, Liu et al. [10] proposed a new approach for joint service
deployment and computational resource allocation based on
parameterized deep Q-networks to minimize the total time
delay of tasks. Jiang et al. [11] proposed a framework for
online joint ofﬂoading and resource allocation under long-
term MEC energy constraints by constructing an energy
loss queue to direct the energy consumption so as to use
computational resources efﬁciently and reduce energy con-
sumption. Liu et al. [12] conducted an in-depth study on
the energy consumption, execution delay and payment cost
of the ofﬂoading process using queuing theory in order to
balance the energy consumption and delay of the system.
In order to minimize the energy consumption of the device
and the execution delay of the task, Bozorgchenani et al.
[13] transformed the task ofﬂoading problem, into a con-
strained multi-objective optimization problem and designed
an evolutionary algorithm to solve the optimization prob-
lem. Since the controller of software-deﬁned network (SDN)
holds the global information of the network, Zhang et al. [14]
proposed a load-balanced task ofﬂoading scheme based on
SDN. Leung et al. [15] utilize collaborative neurodynamic
models to handle diverse optimization objectives simultane-
ously. Hou et al. [15] proposed a reliable task assignment
and reprocessing mechanism that maximizes the reliability
of computational ofﬂoading under time delay constraints,
taking into account that the network may fail. The above
works handle the task execution delay and energy consump-
tion well, but do not consider the waiting time required for
the ofﬂoaded computation tasks before they are scheduled for
execution. As a key technology in IoT application scenarios,
computation ofﬂoading plays an important role in reducing
user execution delay and improving QoS. At this stage, com-
puting ofﬂoading technology is still around a single cloud
computing and edge computing research, but in real life, due
to the progress of urbanization will make the computing envi-
ronment increasingly complex, the amount of computing will
also rise signiﬁcantly. The current relatively mature technol-
ogy is often difﬁcult to be realized in complex environments
due to the lack of consideration of cooperative mechanisms.
Recent advances in constrained system control have
demonstrated various approaches to handling communica-
tion limitations and distributed architectures. Works like
literature [16] developed quantized iterative learning control
with encoding–decoding mechanisms for communication-
constrained systems, while literature [17] proposed adaptive
iterative learning methods for fault estimation in switched
nonlinear reaction–diffusion systems. Although these stud-
ies effectively address spatial–temporal constraints in dis-
tributed control, they primarily focus on continuous system
dynamics rather than discrete task scheduling in cyber-
physical systems. literature [18] further advanced quantized
control strategies for interconnected PDE systems using
mobile measurement approaches, establishing important
paradigms for resource-constrained environments. While
these methodologies share our emphasis on distributed sys-
temoptimizationundercommunicationconstraints,ourwork
diverges by speciﬁcally addressing the unique challenges
of metro operation systems through cloud-edge cooperative
computation rather than pure control theory approaches.
Responding to the above issues, this paper solves the
task co-scheduling problem of MISCS by constructing a
cloud-edge co-computing environment, and a task ofﬂoading
method based on SAGTSA algorithm, an edge cloud coop-
erative architecture and a scheduling optimization method
based on IPN are proposed, which together are used to
accomplish the optimal scheduling of MISCS in complex
environments, and an in-depth study was carried out at three
levels: task ofﬂoading, architecture design and scheduling
optimization, respectively.

SAGTSA-based MISCS cloud edge cooperative
computing offloading method
In order to solve the problem of system service delay
optimization for MISCS in the framework of cloud-side
cooperative, this paper adopts a SAGTSA-based ofﬂoading
method for cloud-side collaborative computing. Aiming at
the problem of premature convergence of traditional genetic
algorithms, the SAGTSA algorithm in this paper has strong
convergence and adaptability by fully combining the global
convergence and adaptability of the simulated annealing
algorithm and the strong climbing ability and high efﬁciency
possessed by the forbidden search strategy. Speciﬁcally, the
chromosome encoding method, the solution updating mech-
anism and the adaptive crossover probability as well as the
adaptive mutation probability are optimized and improved
that enable the system to ﬁnd the optimal computational
ofﬂoading strategy and improve the system time delay effec-
tiveness.

IPN-based algorithmic modeling
The input to the MISCS task scheduling problem in the Cloud
Edge Cooperative Framework is a sequence of tasks and
the output is a combination of the input sequences. There-
fore, a sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) model can be used
to solve this scheduling problem. Considering that the tra-
ditional Seq2Seq model cannot solve the problem that the
output sequence varies with the length of the input sequence,
in this paper, we adopt the Pointer Network (PN) model to
use the Attention Mechanism (AM) as a pointer to select a
member of the input sequence as the output, and replace the
encoder part of the RNN in the structure of the PN with a
one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to
obtain an improved PN and use it for MISCS optimization
of the task scheduling problem.

Conclusion
In this paper, a MISCS cloud-edge cooperative optimiza-
tion scheduling method is proposed. Based on the current
MISCS structure, the SAGTSA algorithm deployed in the
regional centralized control side makes ofﬂoading decisions
for the tasks received by the edge nodes, and the edge-cloud
cooperative processing is utilized to reduce the computa-
tional delay of the tasks, leaving a part of the tasks to be
processed at the edge nodes, and uploading all the remaining
tasks to the cloud center for processing. The designed IPN-
based scheduling optimization method achieves to provide
computing services for as many computing tasks as possible
with the limited computing resources in the server, which
satisﬁes the user’s demand. Simulation results show that the
method proposed in this paper makes the system have high
system timeliness, reduces the impact of system delay, and
effectively reduces the timeout rate of computing tasks, and is
signiﬁcantly better than other algorithms in terms of schedul-
ing effect, which has better timing application feasibility and
contributes to safe scheduling and operation of the metro.
While our approach demonstrates signiﬁcant improve-
ments in scheduling efﬁciency and latency reduction, several
limitations should be noted for practical implementation.
First, the current system assumes ideal network conditions
between edge nodes and cloud centers, and performance
may degrade during network congestion events. Second, the
IPN model requires substantial training data and compu-
tational resources during the initial training phase, though
this is offset by its efﬁcient runtime performance. Third,
the method’s effectiveness depends on accurate task char-
acterization, which could be compromised by sensor noise
or incomplete monitoring data. These limitations suggest
valuable future research directions, including: (1) develop-
ing adaptive network quality prediction models to optimize
ofﬂoading decisions under varying network conditions, (2)
investigating knowledge distillation techniques to create
lighter versions of the IPN model for resource-constrained
edge devices, and (3) exploring robust task characterization
methods that can handle noisy or incomplete input data.
While the proposed method demonstrates signiﬁcant
improvements in cloud-edge cooperative scheduling for
MISCS, several limitations and future research direc-
tions warrant discussion. First, the current implementation
assumes stable network conditions between edge nodes and
cloud centers—future work should investigate robust opti-
mization under dynamic network environments. Second,
the potential integration of quantum-inspired optimization
techniques could further enhance the SAGTSA algorithm’s
performance for ultra-large-scale metro networks. Third, the
application of federated learning approaches could enable
privacy-preserving collaborative learning across different
metro lines while maintaining data locality. Additionally, the
emerging 6G communication technologies may provide new
opportunities to achieve even lower latency and higher reli-
ability in future implementations. These directions present
promising avenues to extend both the theoretical foundations
and practical applications of our framework.
Future research will particularly focus on developing
adaptive versions of the SAGTSA algorithm that can auto-
matically adjust their parameters based on real-time system
loads and network conditions, as well as investigating the
integration of digital twin technologies for more compre-
hensive metro system monitoring and optimization.

Abstract: Metro Integrated Supervision and Control System (MISCS) belongs to the category of integrated automation of electrome- chanical equipment of urban rail transit, through establishing the monitoring and control of each electromechanical equipment system, making its operation within the controllable scope, providing emergency treatment plan and rich information for safe operation and dispatching command, so as to ensure the safety and high efﬁciency of metro operation. rich information, so as to ensure the safety and high efﬁciency of metro operation. Aiming at the operation and scheduling pressure existing in the existing MISCS, a cloud-side cooperative optimization scheduling method for MISCS based on edge computing is designed by taking advantage of the real-time analysis and fast calculation of edge computing technology and relying on the cloud-side cooperative architecture. Using edge-side monitoring data ubiquitous sensing, edge node data feature analysis, panoramic monitoring visualization technology, optimizing the existing MISCS operation mode, designing the operation optimization scheme of the ground body integrated monitoring system applying edge computing technology, and targeting the problem of the current metro integrated monitoring system covering a wide range of areas and having too many tasks, which leads to the system latency being too high, under the cloud-edge cooperative architecture, we propose a simulated annealing-based Simulated-annealing-based Adaptive Genetic Taboo Search Algorithm (SAGTSA) computational ofﬂoading strategy, which enables the scheduling tasks of the MISCS to adaptively adjust the ofﬂoading strategy of migrating to the edge nodes or cloud center. According to the characteristics of task scheduling, a scheduling method based on improved pointer network (IPN) is designed for scheduling ISCS tasks after the computational ofﬂoading strategy based on SAGTSA is proposed. Simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper, the method proposed in this paper has ideal timeliness, is better than other methods in achieving the efﬁciency of scheduling computational tasks, effectively improves the operational performance of MISCS, and helps to enhance the stability of metro operation.
